paper.title: The KL-UCB Algorithm for Bounded Stochastic Bandits and Beyond

settings.name_in_paper: stochastic bandit with rewards bounded in [0,1]
settings.definition_quote: For each $a\in\{1,\dots,K\}$, the rewards $(X_{a,t})_{t\geq 1}$ are independent and bounded in $\Theta = [0,1]$ with common expectation $\mu_a$. The sequences $(X_{a,\cdot})_a$ are independent.

settings.name_in_paper: rewards from a canonical (one-parameter) exponential family
unmapped: learner knows the exponential family (divergence d)
settings.definition_quote: we will assume in this section that, for each arm $a$, the distribution of rewards belongs to a \emph{canonical exponential family}, i.e., that its density with respect to some reference measure can be written as $p_{\theta_a}(x)$ ... $p_{\theta}(x) = \exp\left( x\theta - b(\theta) + c(x) \right)$

algorithms.name: UCB (tuned, exploration log(t)+c log log t)

source.label: th:borneRegret
source.quote: Consider a bandit problem with $K$ arms and independent rewards bounded in $[0,1]$, and denote by $a^*$ an optimal arm. Choosing $c=3$, the regret of the KL-UCB algorithm satisfies: \[\limsup_{n\to\infty} \frac{\E[R_n]}{\log(n)} \leq \sum_{a:\mu_a<\mu_{a^*}} \frac{\mu_{a^*}-\mu_a}{d(\mu_a, \mu_{a^*})}\;.\]

results.notes: Index uses t only (horizon-free), though pseudo-code lists n as input. Expression is the constant multiplying log(T).

bound.regime: any eps > 0, any positive integer T

symbols.kl_i: Bernoulli KL divergence d(mu_a, mu_star) for suboptimal arm a

source.label: th:borneNbplayed
source.quote: Let $\epsilon>0$, and take $c=3$ in Algorithm~\ref{alg:klUCB}. ... For any positive integer $n$, the number of times algorithm KL-UCB chooses arm $a$ is upper-bounded by \[\E[N_n(a)] \leq \frac{\log(n)}{d(\mu_a, \mu_{a^*})}(1+\epsilon) + C_1 \log(\log(n)) + \frac{C_2(\epsilon)}{n^{\beta(\epsilon)}}\;,\]

results.notes: Quantity is expected number of pulls of a suboptimal arm. Constants unspecified (proof says C'_1 <= 7 for one part).
Expected pull count of suboptimal arm, asymptotic.

source.label: prop:betterUCB
source.quote: Consider the UCB algorithm tuned as follows: at step $t>K$, the arm that maximizes the upper-bound $S[a]/N[a] + \sqrt{(\log(t)+c\log\log(t))/(2 N[a])}$ is chosen. Then, for the choice $c=3$, the number of draws of a sub-optimal arm $a$ is upper-bounded as: \E[N_n(a)] \leq \frac{\log(n)}{2(\mu_a-\mu_{a^*})^2}(1+\epsilon) + C_1 \log(\log(n)) + \frac{C_2(\epsilon)}{n^{\beta(\epsilon)}}

results.notes: Proof omitted (mimics KL-UCB proof). Quantity: expected pulls of suboptimal arm. Note: as written in the paper the denominator is 2(mu_a-mu_star)^2 i.e. 2 Delta_i^2.

symbols.KL_i: d(mu_i, mu_star) = KL divergence between family members with means mu_i and mu_star (Lemma dIsKl)

source.quote: Then, all the results stated above apply (as the proofs do not involve the particular form of the function $d$), and in particular~: \[\limsup_{n\to\infty} \frac{\E[R_n]}{\log(n)} \leq \sum_{a:\mu_a<\mu_{a^*}} \frac{\mu_{a^*}-\mu_a}{d(\mu_a, \mu_{a^*})}\;.\]

results.notes: Stated in prose rather than a numbered theorem; relies on Theorem borneDevGen (proof omitted). Matches Lai-Robbins bound via Lemma dIsKl.
